registerPolicy: Cebuano has no du/Sie split: informal ka/nimo/imong second person throughout. Service tone: palihug on lines that make a request (not on every line), full sentences, no slang clitics (bitaw, uy) in learner lines; ta/kita allowed in service lines only when genuinely inclusive of the interlocutor (Magkita ta sa Lunes). Friend tone adds lang/man softeners and inclusive ta/kita freely; host/elder tone keeps full sentences and no slang. Each path names a DEFAULT register; a lesson whose beat names a different interlocutor follows its own scene (P4 lessons 1 and 5 friend; P7 lessons 5, 8 and 9 service), the caption states the role, and within one lesson the register never shifts. Tagalog po/opo/pakisuyo/kayo/hindi banned; 'Ma'am/Sir' allowed only inside them-lines, never learner lines, speech, recall or trophies.
genderSafety: Cebuano has no grammatical gender and no gendered agreement: siya/niya cover all referents, adjectives and verbs never agree. Learner lines never assert the learner's own gender or marital status (no self-labels such as dalaga, ulitawo, asawa, bana as identity). Describing an interlocutor or third person as babaye/lalaki, or using gendered kin terms (lola, iyaan, uyoan), is normal Cebuano and allowed wherever the scene makes it meaningful and respectful. Captions name the role (ang kahera, ang drayber). No gender alternatives and no gendered-token check exist for ceb-PH; the generic validator pass is empty by design.
orthography: Standard Visayan spelling as in A1/A2: ni- completed, nag- progressive, mo-/mag- future/intent; conjunction 'ug', indefinite object marker 'og'; 'kung' canonical, 'kon' accepted only where explicitly listed; glottal-stop hyphen words (bag-o, dad-on, kat-on) allowed in dialogue text only and never in speech tokens, recall answers or trophies. Loanwords keep A2 spellings (reserbasyon, resibo, taksi, kape, selpon). Numbers: native (duha, tulo, lima) for counts, Spanish-derived for clock/money/dates (alas tres, singkwenta, trese) matching A2. DECIDED: (1) fused pronoun forms are written koy/kay/tay without apostrophe in dialogue text (naa koy, wala kay); ko'y is never written; fused forms never appear as speech tokens, recall answers or trophies. (2) mi- completed is never canonical; it may appear only inside a reviewed acceptedVariants full line on a learner turn and never in speech tokens. (3) gi- object focus is recognition-only in them-lines until P6 lesson 4, productive from P6 lesson 4 onward and in P9; -on/i- instruction forms productive from P6 lesson 1 on familiar verbs only.

segmentation.youOne: First learner reply 8-16 words, one or two sentences, connected to the opening; contains the trophy as exact surface word and all three speech tokens; no hyphenated or fused forms among tokens.
segmentation.youTwo: Second learner reply 6-12 words, resolves or continues; reconstructed by 2-3 cloze blanks; must not restate youOne verbatim.
segmentation.chunks: 4-7 chunks, joined by single ASCII space equal youOne exactly. Cut at phrase edges; clitic clusters (na ko, ra gihapon, pa ba, lang ko) never split from their host word; 'kay/kung/aron/bisan' start their clause chunk.
segmentation.speechTokens: Three distinct whole words from youOne: at least one content verb or noun, one connector or aspect-bearing word; never bare clitics (na, ko, ka, ra, ba, lang, pa, man), never hyphenated or fused words (koy/kay/tay). A canonical loanword in its A2 spelling (resibo, reserbasyon, taksi, selpon) is a valid token; only unanchored alternative spellings (taxi, Wi-Fi) are excluded. Threshold 0.55 and the established B1 recording duration 15 s; revisit only after a measured pilot.
segmentation.trophyAnchoring: Trophy is the exact lowercase surface word in youOne and in trophyWord.example; Cebuano affixation changes surface (sugod vs nagsugod), so verb trophies are the affixed form actually spoken (nagdali, nisakay, gisagol) or a root that stands bare natively as noun or stative predicate (sa sugod 'at the start', bukal na 'already boiling', wala pay sulbad 'no solution yet', hangyo ko nga 'my request is'). No substring matches: 'una' must be the word, not inside 'unang'. Never strip or add affixes or clitics to satisfy the validator; if the taught form is affixed, the trophy is the affixed word.
segmentation.acceptedInput: Only explicitly reviewed spelling variants per turn (kung/kon, og/ug, taksi/taxi, Wi-Fi/wifi, ni-/mi- where listed). No clitic dropping, no synonym substitution, no automatic normalization beyond NFC and casefold.

knownTraps: dili negates future/habitual/adjectives/intent (dili ko mobayad, dili mahal); wala negates past, existence and progressive, and the verb after wala takes the mo-/mag- base form or the ka-/naka- abilitative, never ni-/nag- in canonical lines: Wala ko mobayad (I did not pay), Wala ko katulog og maayo (I could not sleep well), Wala pa ko mangaon, walay tubig. The dili/wala pair is never interchangeable in cloze, and the prefix after wala is not what marks past: wala itself does.

Clitics attach to the first full word of the clause, but there is no single universal stack: monosyllabic na/pa/ra/lang normally precede the pronoun (Nahuman na ko; Mangutana lang ko; Mohulat ra ko), ba follows na/pa and precedes the pronoun in questions (Nakakaon na ba ka?; Mahimo ba ko mangutana?), while ko lang / ko ra also occurs natively after longer hosts (Mohulat ko lang diri). Canonical lines use the ordering of these examples; a reviewer flags order semantically, never auto-reorders, and an order not attested in the examples is a review item, not an automatic error.
ni- (A2 canonical) vs mi- completed: keep ni- canonical in all canonical lines; mi- only as reviewed accepted variant, never in speech tokens.
Object-focus gi-/-on/i- changes word order and pronoun forms (gihugas nako vs naghugas ko); do not mix focuses inside one clause.
'kay' is both subordinator (because) and topic marker (ako kay); cloze connector blanks must make the reading unambiguous.
'nga' linker vs 'ka' numeral linker (usa ka tawo, tawo nga taas): never swap.
Trophy surface: forbidden list is trophy-only; forbidden words (kabalo, gusto, unya) remain usable in dialogue, just never as B1 trophies.
Tagalog bleed: po, opo, pakisuyo, kayo, hindi, kasi, kumain, magkano; also careless calques of German tense ('Ich habe gewartet' needs naghulat/nihulat, not naa ko).
Hyphenated glottal words (bag-o, kat-on, dad-on) are correct spelling but excluded from speech, recall, trophies; prefer hyphen-free synonyms in those slots.
'kung' doubles as if-condition and indirect-question introducer; stage the two readings in separate paths (P3 vs P5) and never cloze on it where both fit.
Spanish-derived time and money numbers must stay in their A2 forms; do not introduce English digits as words.
mechanicalValidationRules: Trophies: lowercase, single token, NFC+casefold unique against A1, A2 and all B1; not in forbiddenTrophies; no hyphen, apostrophe, digit, capital; must appear as whole word in dialogue[1].targetText and trophyWord.example.

Dialogue tuple4 order: them, learner, them, learner; learner turns 8-16 and 6-12 words; sceneCaption.de and .en each contain dialogue[0].targetText verbatim inside quotation marks and do not contain dialogue[2].targetText as a full line; quoted target text inside a German or English caption is expected and never flagged. Whether the caption foreshadows the complication of dialogue[2] is a semantic review item, not a substring check.
Chunks joined by one ASCII space equal dialogue[1].targetText exactly; 4-7 chunks; 6-8 terms.
speakRequired has exactly 3 distinct tokens, each a whole word of dialogue[1], none in a stoplist of clitics, none containing '-' or an apostrophe.

Cloze: 2-3 blank parts, each exactly 4 distinct choices with exactly one answer; join of parts equals dialogue[3].targetText; kind in form/connector/choice; cue (single string, root + aspect, e.g. 'bayad, completed') present only on form blanks; every answer is a whole inflected word or a phrase of at most 3 space-separated units, never a bound morpheme, bare prefix or anything containing '-' or an apostrophe; no blank whose answer is a bare pronoun, clitic or article.
Recall: before+answer+after equals dialogue[1].targetText; fallbackChoices exactly 4 distinct, answer included, answer is a content word of 3+ letters.
Pattern: 2-3 examples, highlight is a contiguous substring of its targetText; at least one example equals dialogue[1] or dialogue[3] targetText.
Every base text field has both de and en; pedagogicalGoal is a German string; no en text in .de fields (heuristic: common English function words).
Banned tokens anywhere in target text: po, opo, pakisuyo, kayo, hindi, kasi, magkano, kumain.

Flag for review: 'dili' immediately before ni-/nag-/naka-/gi-/naa; 'wala' immediately before ni-/nag- (colloquial, not canonical). 'wala' + mo-/mag- and 'wala' + ka-/naka- are the regular negated past and pass.

Aspect license per learner turn: a completed base tense (de Perfekt/Praeteritum, en past) is licensed by ni-/naka-/gi-/na- in the same turn, by wala + mo-/mag-/ka- negated past, or by nag- when the same turn or the directly preceding them-line carries a past frame (ganina, gahapon, kaniadto, sauna, gabii, a ni-/gi- clause); a future base (de Futur or Praesens mit Zeitangabe, en will/going to) requires mo-/mag-/ma- or a future time word (ugma, sunod semana) or a kung/aron/basta clause in the same turn; unta alone licenses only wish/irrealis (de Konjunktiv II, en would/wish), never plain future.
semanticReviewRules: Each learner turn is a real reply to the preceding them-line; dialogue[2] adds new information (complication, interest or counter-offer), not a repeat.
Learner never asserts staff-only decisions (refund granted, room changed); learner requests or accepts with modification.
Focus and aspect choices match the pathʼs staged productive set; recognition-only forms appear only in them-lines.
German is idiomatic and not a gloss of English; English is not a gloss of German; both carry the same aspect meaning the target licenses.

Register coherence is checked per lesson against the scene named in its beat: service scenes use palihug on request lines and neutral full sentences, with ta/kita only when genuinely inclusive; friend and host scenes may use ta/kita and lang; the path register is the default and the exception lessons listed in registerPolicy (P4 L1/L5, P7 L5/L8/L9) are reviewed as their own scene.

Cloze distractors are grammatically or contextually impossible in that exact slot, never near-synonyms or spelling variants: apan/pero, kung/kon, og/ug, lang/ra, ni-/mi- forms must never co-occur as choices; the pairs dili/wala, kung/aron, bisan/apan, nga/ka, sa/og are each checked to admit exactly one native answer in context.
whyThisWord explains reuse value and the exact surface form taught, in both locales.
No Tagalog, no Hiligaynon forms, no invented loanwords; loanwords must match A2 spelling precedents.
P9 and P10 lessons visibly recycle at least two earlier families each; check the recycling map is honored, not only stated.
requiredSchemaExtensions: Register ceb-PH in the offline Latin-target list (currently five targets) so B1 offline bundles build; no new field shapes.

Register ceb-PH B1 in the existing native-check tooling (banned-token list, trophy uniqueness against the frozen forbiddenTrophies list plus all B1 trophies, whole-word anchoring, caption quote check); all checks run on the existing schema.

Dialogue learner turns only: OPTIONAL acceptedVariants string[] of reviewed exact full-line spellings (kon for kung, og/ug, taksi/taxi, mi- for ni- where listed); no token-level rules, no auto-generation.

No other schema change: cloze cue stays a single string present only on form blanks, trophyWord.example stays a string, pattern.rule stays a string, meaning and whyThisWord stay {de,en} as in A2. Speech thresholds and recording seconds are source audit metadata, not runtime schema: ceb-PH B1 uses threshold 0.55 and the established B1 recording duration 15 s.

Coworker asks about the storm day; you cooked while rain fell; she asks about power.

Friend notices your wet bag; you explain what happened on the jeepney; she asks damage.
Cousin asks how the fiesta began; you describe the parade start with sugod as a noun (Sa sugod naglinya ang mga banda sa plasa, dayon nilakaw sila paingon sa simbahan); he asks the ending.
Landlady asks why you were late; because of traffic you walked; she asks from where.
Vendor asks if you lived here before; you describe life back then; she asks changes.
Driver asks why you ran; you hurried for the last trip; he asks if you caught it.

lessons.beat: You hope the room could face the sea; receptionist offers garden side; you accept with discount.
If it rains tomorrow, could the tour move? Guide offers morning slot; you adjust.
